audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Manasseh and Amon reigns, child-through-fire, innocent blood, judgment oracle, palace assassination, and popular retaliation narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for child kingship, restoration of high places, Baal/Asherah and heavenly-host worship, child-through-fire, divination and spirit-practitioner terminology, temple pluralization, prophetic collective-judgment rhetoric, Manasseh's shedding of innocent blood, Amon's assassination, retaliatory execution of conspirators, and Josiah's succession.

verses.restored: Twelve years old was Manasseh when he became king, and fifty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Hephzibah.

familiar.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hephzibah.

modern.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-five years. His mother’s name was Hephzibah.

original.text: בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֨ים עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֥ם אִמּ֖וֹ חֶפְצִי בָֽהּ

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH, according to abominations of nations whom YHWH dispossessed from before children of Israel.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, after the abominations of the heathen, whom the LORD cast out before the children of Israel.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD by following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: He rebuilt high places Hezekiah his father destroyed, raised altars for Baal, made an Asherah as Ahab king of Israel had done, bowed to all host of heavens, and served them.

familiar.text: For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he reared up altars for Baal, and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Israel; and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.

modern.text: For he rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed, and he raised up altars for Baal. He made an Asherah pole, as King Ahab of Israel had done, and he worshiped and served all the host of heaven.

original.text: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִבַּ֖ד חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּ֨קֶם מִזְבְּחֹ֜ת לַבַּ֗עַל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֲשֵׁרָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה אַחְאָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ֙ לְכָל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ד אֹתָֽם

verses.restored: He built altars in house of YHWH, concerning which YHWH said, In Jerusalem I will put my name.

familiar.text: And he built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD said, In Jerusalem will I put my name.

modern.text: Manasseh also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem I will put My Name.”

original.text: וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּחֹ֖ת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת שְׁמִֽי

verses.restored: He built altars for all host of heavens in two courts of house of YHWH.

familiar.text: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

modern.text: In both courtyards of the house of the LORD, he built altars to all the host of heaven.

original.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: He made his son pass through fire, practiced soothsaying and omens, and dealt with a medium and spirit-knowers. He multiplied doing evil in eyes of YHWH, provoking him.

familiar.text: And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.

modern.text: He sacrificed his own son in the fire, practiced sorcery and divination, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

original.text: וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אֶת בְּנוֹ֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעוֹנֵ֣ן וְנִחֵ֔שׁ וְעָ֥שָׂה א֖וֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִ֑ים הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִֽיס

verses.restored: He set carved image of Asherah he had made in house concerning which YHWH said to David and Solomon his son, In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all tribes of Israel, I will put my name for all time.

familiar.text: And he set a graven image of the grove that he had made in the house, of which the LORD said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

modern.text: Manasseh even took the carved Asherah pole he had made and set it up in the temple, of which the LORD had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever.

original.text: וַיָּ֕שֶׂם אֶת פֶּ֥סֶל הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה בַּבַּ֗יִת אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל דָּוִד֙ וְאֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ בַּבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אָשִׂ֥ים אֶת שְׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם

verses.restored: I will not again make foot of Israel wander from land I gave their fathers, if only they guard to do according to all I commanded them and according to all Torah my servant Moses commanded them.

familiar.text: Neither will I make the feet of Israel move any more out of the land which I gave their fathers; only if they will observe to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that my servant Moses commanded them.

modern.text: I will never again cause the feet of the Israelites to wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they are careful to do all I have commanded them—the whole Law that My servant Moses commanded them.”

original.text: וְלֹ֣א אֹסִ֗יף לְהָנִיד֙ רֶ֣גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִן הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַֽאֲבוֹתָ֑ם רַ֣ק אִם יִשְׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ים וּלְכָל הַ֨תּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם עַבְדִּ֥י מֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: But they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do more evil than nations YHWH destroyed from before children of Israel.

familiar.text: But they hearkened not: and Manasseh seduced them to do more evil than did the nations whom the LORD destroyed before the children of Israel.

modern.text: But the people did not listen and Manasseh led them astray, so that they did greater evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites. Manasseh’s Idolatries Rebuked (2 Chronicles 33:10–20)

original.text: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּתְעֵ֤ם מְנַשֶּׁה֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֶת הָרָ֔ע מִן הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: YHWH spoke through his servants the prophets, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake by his servants the prophets, saying,

modern.text: And the LORD spoke through His servants the prophets, saying,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Because Manasseh king of Judah did these abominations, doing more evil than all Amorites before him, and caused Judah also to sin with his idols,

familiar.text: Because Manasseh king of Judah hath done these abominations, and hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols:

modern.text: “Since Manasseh king of Judah has committed all these abominations, acting more wickedly than the Amorites who preceded him, and with his idols has caused Judah to sin,

original.text: יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ הַתֹּעֵב֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה הֵרַ֕ע מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר עָשׂ֥וּ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּחֲטִ֥א גַֽם אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּגִלּוּלָֽיו

verses.restored: therefore thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: Look, I am bringing evil upon Jerusalem and Judah, such that both ears of everyone hearing it shall tingle.

familiar.text: Therefore thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Behold, I am bringing such evil upon Jerusalem and Judah, that whosoever heareth of it, both his ears shall tingle.

modern.text: this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I am bringing such calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah that the news will reverberate in the ears of all who hear it.

original.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא רָעָ֔ה עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וִֽיהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ כָּל שמעיו תִּצַּ֖לְנָה שְׁתֵּ֥י אָזְנָֽיו

verses.restored: I will stretch over Jerusalem measuring line of Samaria and plummet of house of Ahab. I will wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping and turning it upon its face.

familiar.text: And I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down.

modern.text: I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measuring line used against Samaria and the plumb line used against the house of Ahab, and I will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes out a bowl—wiping it and turning it upside down.

original.text: וְנָטִ֣יתִי עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֵ֚ת קָ֣ו שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְאֶת מִשְׁקֹ֖לֶת בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וּמָחִ֨יתִי אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם כַּֽאֲשֶׁר יִמְחֶ֤ה אֶת הַצַּלַּ֨חַת֙ מָחָ֔ה וְהָפַ֖ךְ עַל פָּנֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: I will abandon remnant of my inheritance and give them into hand of their enemies; they shall become prey and plunder to all their enemies,

familiar.text: And I will forsake the remnant of mine inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies; and they shall become a prey and a spoil to all their enemies;

modern.text: So I will forsake the remnant of My inheritance and deliver them into the hands of their enemies. And they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,

original.text: וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֗י אֵ֚ת שְׁאֵרִ֣ית נַחֲלָתִ֔י וּנְתַתִּ֖ים בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָי֥וּ לְבַ֛ז וְלִמְשִׁסָּ֖ה לְכָל אֹיְבֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: because they did evil in my eyes and provoked me from day their fathers came out of Egypt even to this day.

familiar.text: Because they have done that which was evil in my sight, and have provoked me to anger, since the day their fathers came forth out of Egypt, even unto this day.

modern.text: because they have done evil in My sight and have provoked Me to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day.’”

original.text: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶת הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וַיִּהְי֥וּ מַכְעִסִ֖ים אֹתִ֑י מִן הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֤וּ אֲבוֹתָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Moreover Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from mouth to mouth, besides his sin by which he caused Judah to sin, doing evil in eyes of YHWH.

familiar.text: Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another; beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the LORD.

modern.text: Moreover, Manasseh shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from end to end, in addition to the sin that he had caused Judah to commit, doing evil in the sight of the LORD.

original.text: וְגַם֩ דָּ֨ם נָקִ֜י שָׁפַ֤ךְ מְנַשֶּׁה֙ הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר מִלֵּ֥א אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם פֶּ֣ה לָפֶ֑ה לְבַ֤ד מֵֽחַטָּאתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱטִ֣יא אֶת יְהוּדָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Manasseh, all he did, and his sin that he sinned, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Manasseh, along with all his accomplishments and the sin that he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י מְנַשֶּׁה֙ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְחַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֑א הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Manasseh lay with his fathers and was buried in garden of his house, in garden of Uzza. Amon his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza: and Amon his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried in his palace garden, the garden of Uzza. And his son Amon reigned in his place. Amon Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 33:21–25)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּגַן בֵּית֖וֹ בְּגַן עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Twenty-two years old was Amon when he became king, and two years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

familiar.text: Amon was twenty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.

modern.text: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem two years. His mother’s name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz; she was from Jotbah.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מְשֻׁלֶּ֥מֶת בַּת חָר֖וּץ מִן יָטְבָֽה

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH, as Manasseh his father had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה אָבִֽיו

familiar.text: And he walked in all the way that his father walked in, and served the idols that his father served, and worshipped them:

modern.text: He walked in all the ways of his father, and he served and worshiped the idols his father had served.

original.text: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּכָל הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר הָלַ֣ךְ אָבִ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֗ד אֶת הַגִּלֻּלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָבַ֣ד אָבִ֔יו וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לָהֶֽם

modern.text: He abandoned the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Amon which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Amon, along with his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָמ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: They buried him in his grave in garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: And he was buried in his sepulchre in the garden of Uzza: and Josiah his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And he was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיִּקְבְֹּ֥ר אֹת֛וֹ בִּקְבֻרָת֖וֹ בְּגַן עֻזָּ֑א וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

translation_notes: Manasseh begins ruling at twelve. A child king remains vulnerable to court systems, inherited institutions, and adult advisers; youth does not remove later accountability or prove children should wield sovereign power.
Making his son pass through fire is child abuse or sacrifice. No parental, royal, or religious authority can make a child's body an offering.
Medium and spirit-knower vocabulary describes ancient religious specialists. The text may not support witch-hunts, occult panic, misogyny, or violence toward contemporary spiritual practitioners.
The narrator condemns Manasseh's placement of other sacred practices in the temple. This covenantal polemic may not authorize attacks on other religions or forced religious uniformity.
The wiping-dish image and abandonment of the remnant express collective destruction. Such rhetoric is morally dangerous and may not justify punishing a population for a ruler's acts.
Verse 16 identifies Manasseh's abundant shedding of innocent blood as central to his reign. The victims remain unnamed but must not disappear behind disputes about ritual.
The claim that Manasseh exceeded the Amorites is ancient ethnic polemic and cannot become contempt toward modern peoples or justification of conquest.
Amon is assassinated by palace servants, and the people then execute the conspirators. Neither murder nor retaliatory killing supplies due process.
The mothers Hephzibah and Meshullemeth are named as lineage markers, not causes of their sons' actions.
Chronicles preserves a substantially different Manasseh tradition including captivity, repentance, and reform; the witnesses require separate treatment rather than forced harmonization.
safety_note: Do not normalize child sacrifice, persecute spiritual practitioners or minority religions, blame an entire population for a king's crimes, erase Manasseh's victims, glorify assassination, or celebrate retaliatory execution. Center children, innocent blood, institutional accountability, and the limits of dynastic and prophetic punishment theology.
